N2 Hell Run

By: Liz Fish | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The N2 approaching CT International airport is a crime hot spot - how do you stop this scourge? Will a R180 million rand wall make a difference?

Unique Selling Point:
The N2 approaching Cape Town International airport and the R300 have long been described as “The Hell Run” as far back as 2005 and the City of Cape Town and Sanral have attempted to deal with the problem. But it remains one of the most dangerous stretches of road that even law enforcement is fearful to hang around. 2025 was a bumper holiday season for Cape Town- and everybody cashed in- and so did the gangs of kids attacking passing motorist and motorcyclists.

Summary:
There are 285 CCTV camera monitored 24/7. Concrete fences constructed which have been systematically torn down. The pedestrian bridges covered with wire” cages”. 37 new officers deployed in October 2025, increased number of patrol officers and vehicles and a ghost squad in place. Now they are talking about constructing R180 million rand wall. SANRAL has already begun constructing a wall on the R300 as “a Pilot" – but this is one of the most elusive problems to police as perpetrators pop up and disappear within minutes, any time of the day or night.

Further information:
There really is no time that is safe, even driving into or leaving the airport off the N2 is no longer safe. Often its young kids standing on the side of the road, looking like they are waiting to cross, at the last minute they pull a rock out and hurl it at the car or motorbike. Now they stepping into the road with firearms pointed at the motorist.
6 arrests were made this week, but this is a scourge that isn't going away.
We will travel with the ghost squad for a late shift. Get the personal stories of the officers about the threat to their lives and the trauma of the victims. Speak to victims who describe their ordeals, and the help they did or did not receive, both motorists and motor bike victims. Tow truck drivers and Community policing forums. JP Smith has confirmed an interview about the Cities efforts, (he downplays the problem) and also the controversial plans to construct a R180 million wall.


Extra Budget Items:
May have to travel to JHB to speak to victims

Expert:
Mr. JP Smith

(Upsound )“10-4 South Bound, 29 is on location, Hotel 29
(Erin) A car has broken down on Cape Town’s notorious N2.
(Erin) A specialized traffic enforcement team is dispatched. Time - is of the essence.
(Upsound ) Able to confirm its N2
(Erin) “Are you ok, what happened?
(Unknown ) “We are short of fuel”
(Erin) :Showe
(Erin) It's late at night and this is a pretty terrible place to break down or run out of fuel,
(Erin) This is the Hell Run —a stretch of highway that cuts across the Cape Flats, between Cape Town International Airport and Somerset West - flanked by poor communities - with high crime rates.
Now, the city is planning to build a multi-million Rand wall across parts of the highway. But, with flashpoints appearing on other routes, will it solve this crisis?
(Erin) “ Do you think the wall is going to make your job easier”
(Officer) It might slow them down, but I doubt it will stop them completely
FADE
( Erin) Cape Town’s main arteries have become hunting grounds. Anyone can fall victim - at any time of day.
(Erin) It was 4pm on a busy Sunday. Paul and Tammy Treleven were on the N2, to catch their flight home to Johannesburg
(Paul) And I just got into the left lane, and I saw a figure pop up next to the highway behind the anchor barrier, and I saw an object coming towards the car.
(Tammy): I wanted to get something out of my handbag and reached down, and as I did that, I just heard this massive explosion, and then it felt like somebody had slapped me through the face really, really hard. It was just really sore and stringy,
(Erin) A rock had smashed through the passenger window, hitting the headrest where Tammy had been, seconds before. Her face was sliced by the glass, and her cornea damaged.
(Erin) Paul, a retired paramedic, kept his composure as a car carrying two men,pulled up alongside them.
(Paul) I looked at them and they started shouting at me that I'd killed a kid. I looked behind and I saw the rock on the on the floor behind Tammy seat. so then I said to Tammy these guys are in on this I am not stopping, then they swerved in front of us. They put the hazards on, and they started slowing down to stop us on the highway. So I evaded them into the fast lane, and then I accelerated to the airport
(Tammy) I kept screaming at him, please stop the car, please stop the car. I can't see Had that rock hit me on the side of the head, it would have killed me instantly.
(Erin) Tammy was saved by a split-second distraction.
(Erin) The Treleven’s were surprised they received no warnings when they landed, or collected their hired car.
(Erin) “Tourism in Cape Town is booming, last year 11 million people landed in this airport, 1,12 million in December alone
(Erin) Yet most arrive completely unaware of the danger waiting on the final stretch of their journey.
(Erin) While investigating this story we’re disturbed to discover just how close to the airport some of these attacks happen, with some incidents stretching back years.
(Erin) By the time you get here you really think you are home and dry, the airport is in sight, so you let down your guard
(Erin) On a Sunday afternoon, around three years ago, a woman in her 20’s was rounding the final bend of the airport approach road, when she saw a man standing on the verge, apparently waiting to cross.
But he had other intentions.
(Erin) The rock shattered her lower jaw and all this time later, the damage remains. She’s unable to eat properly and is still too traumatised to agree to an interview.
(Erin) This year another woman was attacked less than a kilometre from the airport.
(Erin) “ After dropping off her sister at the airport around noon on New Years day, she turned this corner towards Somerset West and slowed down as a man walked into the road
(Erin) Unwilling to show her face, she describes what happened next. We’ve disguised her voice in this recording.
(Anonymous women) ” he was walking towards my car and he was pointing the gun at my windscreen right in front of me. I just instinctively ducked and I just put my foot flat on the accelerator and I got the hell out of there….. I was too scared to look at him properly in the face in case he shot me in my face, it was over in a minute…..
(Erin) Most of these cases go unreported and the victims are left feeling isolated
(Paul): When I was flying back to Johannesburg. I thought to myself, I'm not going to leave this because this happens to people and just get swept under the carpet all the time, and people aren't actually aware of the dangers around Cape Town
(Erin) Paul emailed every authority he could, threatened an international media campaign, and started a WhatsApp group for the victims of attacks on the N2 and nearby R300.
( Paul ) Maybe by us reaching out to other victims, we can create our own stats and show the government what's actually going on.
(Erin) In the past year, the City of Cape Town has overseen a dedicated freeway safety program — adding 37 additional metro officers to patrol N2 hotspots.
(J.P Smith:) That has allowed us in the last seven months to get to about 148 arrests along that particular section of freeway.
(Erin) In addition, new technology is also being deployed. It’s shown to us by J.P Smith, Mayoral Committee Member for Safety and Security. He says, of the 8500 call-outs on the main freeways, 85 percent were for mechanical failures — only a fraction were criminal attacks.
(JP Smith) 1% of the incidents are crime related. If I look at our festive season, this last festive season, we had nine incidents compared to 18 incidents the previous festive season.
(Erin) Given that many incidents go unreported, these stats might not give the full picture.
(Erin) Smith says various authorities, including metro and traffic police and disaster management, are now integrated, and they’re coordinated and dispatched directly from this Traffic Management Centre.
(JP Smith) So at any given time now there are at least a few vehicles on the N2 and R300, especially around the hotspots, uh, to make sure that there is an operational presence. Some of those vehicles are unmarked, so sometimes people will not be aware of the full extent of operational response because the vehicles are not all marked vehicles.
(Erin) But criminals appear and disappear within minutes - and bikers are especially vulnerable. This victim has asked to stay anonymous.
(Biker) “Coming towards the bridge I noticed a guy standing at the side of the road, and I thought he was just waiting to cross, at the very last minute he had a stone and just threw it…
(Erin) The attack was captured on his helmet camera.
(Biker) “I was going at about 100kms an hour at the time and I had no chance to react, and ahh, it just hit the front wheel”
(Erin) Miraculously he got up and walked back to his bike - but the ordeal wasn’t over,
(Biker) “Three young guys came from across the road, and they were trying to take my stuff, within seconds after that is when the truck showed up, the guys that came to help me
(Erin) “ And they were like get out now
(Biker) “Ja they were They said get out of this area as quickly as you can so they helped me do that
(Erin) He had to replaced his bike and gear - and now keeps a close watch on safety alerts.
(Biker) The majority of them basically say, I just don't use that road. You know, just use a different road. But, um, it's getting difficult because, um, what I've noticed recently is we're starting to run out of roads. Initially it was don't use the R 300. Now it's don't use the R 300 or the N2. Now it's don't use the N7. And now more recently we're having attacks on the N1. So which road are we supposed to use?
(JP Smith) It is not possible to securitize those full lengths of those long freeways everywhere. We are making sure that we have a significantly enhanced presence. Operationally. You can only take that so far. Faster response of vehicles. Better use of CCTV cameras. More response vehicles. That will take you to a certain point. But we do need the accompanying engineering solutions.
(Erin) Among the engineering solutions are a three-meter-high wall at various hotspots and an upgrade of the N2.
The price tag is around R114 million but the message it sends rather than the cost, is dividing opinion. Critics argue that it’s an attempt to keep poverty from view.
(Erin) “ Not without its controversy, though. And the spatial politics of Cape Town are distinct from Western European Cities or those in North America
(JP Smith) It is normal to ensure that in a freeway, vehicles are moving in high speed, that they are not animals or pedestrians. In those road reserves, we have the added dynamic of trying to ensure that motorists are secure. And those engineering solutions are going to be essential
(Erin) After years of standoffs between the various authorities as to who is responsible for motorist safety - upgrades are happening.
This wall for example was constructed by the National Roads Agency. It’s lower than the one now proposed by the City.
(Erin) ” SANRAL has built this wall on the edge of the R300 next to a high crime area in an effort to combat the problem
(Erin) Hello, Did you pick us up on the cameras?
(Jacobs) Yes, we did,
(Erin) But this wall, is it making any difference?
(Jacobs) To me the wall makes a difference because it's a solid structure. This one over here, they can still cut with some type of equipment, and yes we do get a lot of people that get knocked over on the road….. but we're just happy that the road is safe because it's easy for crime to come over from that side onto the road
(Tammy) “When it happened to us, we realized how close we came to dying that day.
(Erin) In a city where scores of people are killed in gang violence, building a wall along a highway was always going to be controversial. But few would disagree, that proper police resourcing, political will and social upliftment, are the only long-term solutions.

Promo (Erin) Under the shroud of darkness we join the City of Cape Town’s ghost squad on the notorious hell run of the N2
VO: Will a wall in the hot spots solve the problem?
(Erin) “Do you think the wall is going to make your job easier
(Officer) It might slow them down but I doubt it will stop them completely
Promo 2 (Paul): I was expecting to see the side of her face taken off, if it was a fraction of a second earlier, it would have been a full impact in the face
(Erin) Stonings on the N2 around Cape Town International airport terrorize visitors and commuters alike
(Annonomous)“He was pointing the gun at my windscreen right in front of me. I just instinctively ducked and I just put my foot on the accelerator and got the hell out of there….
Promo 3 (Erin) Overhead cameras, cages over pedestrians crossings, barriers and more officers on patrol- the major highways around Cape Town remain under siege
(Biker) I was going at about 100km an hour at the time, there was no time to react, when, uh, when the rock hit…, the front wheel, I went flying over the over the front of the bike.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): The N2 approaching CT International airport is a crime hot spot - how do you stop this scourge? Will a R180 million rand wall make a difference?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: The N2 approaching Cape Town International airport and the R300 have long been described as “The Hell Run” as far back as 2005 and the City of Cape Town and Sanral have attempted to deal with the problem. But it remains one of the most dangerous stretches of road that even law enforcement is fearful to hang around. 2025 was a bumper holiday season for Cape Town- and everybody cashed in- and so did the gangs of kids attacking passing motorist and motorcyclists.
metadata.Summary: There are 285 CCTV camera monitored 24/7. Concrete fences constructed which have been systematically torn down. The pedestrian bridges covered with wire” cages”. 37 new officers deployed in October 2025, increased number of patrol officers and vehicles and a ghost squad in place. Now they are talking about constructing R180 million rand wall. SANRAL has already begun constructing a wall on the R300 as “a Pilot" – but this is one of the most elusive problems to police as perpetrators pop up and disappear within minutes, any time of the day or night.
metadata.Further information: There really is no time that is safe, even driving into or leaving the airport off the N2 is no longer safe. Often its young kids standing on the side of the road, looking like they are waiting to cross, at the last minute they pull a rock out and hurl it at the car or motorbike. Now they stepping into the road with firearms pointed at the motorist. 6 arrests were made this week, but this is a scourge that isn't going away. We will travel with the ghost squad for a late shift. Get the personal stories of the officers about the threat to their lives and the trauma of the victims. Speak to victims who describe their ordeals, and the help they did or did not receive, both motorists and motor bike victims. Tow truck drivers and Community policing forums. JP Smith has confirmed an interview about the Cities efforts, (he downplays the problem) and also the controversial plans to construct a R180 million wall.
